name: Blue Editoria : Content workflow
author: webmaster-wordpress.com

sections.description:
Blue Editoria : Content workflow helps WordPress teams analyze existing content, prepare SEO and GEO-friendly content workflows, manage internal linking, edit content faster, and automate editorial tasks from a guided WordPress admin interface.

The plugin is designed for site owners, agencies, editors and SEO teams who need a simple workflow without turning WordPress into a complex page builder. It guides the user through setup, content scanning, analyzed content review, spreadsheet-style editing, internal linking, content campaigns, metadata suggestions, schema preparation, and AI-assisted content generation.

Main features

  • Guided dashboard with simple next-step recommendations.
  • Content scanning for selected post types.
  • Content library with SEO, GEO and internal linking indicators.
  • Spreadsheet-style content view for fast review and bulk workflows.
  • Internal linking suggestions, validation and link inventory.
  • Campaign workflow for creating and improving content.
  • AI-assisted content generation and regeneration from existing content context.
  • Meta title and meta description suggestions.
  • Schema and rich result readiness helpers.
  • llms.txt preparation tools for AI discovery workflows.
  • Multilingual organization for WPML, Polylang or language-aware sites.
  • Admin notifications limited to plugin actions.
  • Logs, diagnostics and performance cache helpers for safer operation.

Built for WordPress workflows

Blue Editoria : Content workflow uses WordPress post types, fields, taxonomies and content APIs. It does not create new fields automatically and does not replace your theme. The plugin is meant to help you analyze, organize and improve content while keeping control inside WordPress.

External service disclosure

Some features connect to the Blue Editoria : Content workflow service hosted on blue-editoria.com.

Service name:

  • Blue Editoria : Content workflow service.

The service is used for:

  • Service account connection and site authorization for remote processing.
  • Credit balance and usage history for remote AI requests.
  • AI generation, regeneration and structured suggestions processed outside WordPress.

A service account is not required to install, activate or use the local WordPress features of the plugin. A configured service key is required only when the user deliberately triggers connected remote features such as AI generation, credit balance, usage history or account-backed generation requests.

Service endpoint:

  • https://blue-editoria.com/wp-json/seo-license-manager/v1/

Data sent to the service may include:

  • Site URL, installation ID, plugin version and WordPress version.
  • Service key and site connection token when configured.
  • User prompts and selected content data required for the requested generation.
  • Content titles, excerpts, selected post content, field mappings, post type context, target language, SEO/GEO instructions and internal linking context.
  • Usage metadata such as generation action, status, token counts and credit usage.

Each successful remote AI request may consume service credits. Editorial outputs are charged from the number of words actually generated (one generated word equals one credit). Assistants, audits and suggestions that do not produce final editorial content are charged from actual token usage (100 tokens equal one credit, rounded up). The central service validates and applies the final charge, while the plugin displays the confirmed usage and remaining balance. A failed remote request consumes no credit, and failed local validation never modifies WordPress content. The service may retain the generation identifier, usage metadata and generated response needed to prevent duplicate billing, replay an interrupted response and provide usage history.

Data received from the service may include:

  • Service account status.
  • Credit balance and usage information.
  • AI-generated text, structured JSON suggestions or generation errors.

No third-party AI provider key is exposed in the browser by the plugin. AI requests are routed through the documented service endpoint when the user triggers an AI feature.

You can disable outgoing AI service calls with the aiscb_allow_external_saas_calls filter. AI generation features will not work while service calls are disabled.

Service terms and privacy information:

  • Service website: https://blue-editoria.com/
  • Account portal: https://blue-editoria.com/mon-compte/
  • Credits: https://blue-editoria.com/credits/
  • Service plans: https://blue-editoria.com/tarifs/
  • Support: https://blue-editoria.com/contact/
  • Terms and privacy: https://blue-editoria.com/conditions-et-confidentialites/
  • Privacy policy: https://blue-editoria.com/conditions-et-confidentialites/
  • Terms of service: https://blue-editoria.com/conditions-et-confidentialites/

Privacy

Blue Editoria : Content workflow stores plugin settings, scan state, generated suggestions, logs, local usage history and model data in the WordPress database.

When connected AI features are used, the plugin sends the minimum data needed for the selected action to the service endpoint listed above. Administrators should review the provider terms and privacy information and inform site users according to their own privacy obligations.

Developer Notes

Useful filters include:

  • aiscb_detected_fields
  • aiscb_available_components
  • aiscb_generation_payload
  • aiscb_generated_html
  • aiscb_generated_css
  • aiscb_activation_rules
  • aiscb_allow_external_saas_calls

Generated frontend CSS is scoped with the aiscb- prefix to reduce theme conflicts. The plugin should not load admin assets globally outside its own screens.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install the plugin ZIP from the WordPress admin.
  2. Activate “Blue Editoria : Content workflow” from the Plugins screen.
  3. Open “Blue Editoria : Content workflow” in the WordPress admin menu.
  4. Configure the content types you want to analyze.
  5. Connect your service account from the account screen if you want to use connected AI generation features.
  6. Run the first site scan, then open the content library to review analyzed content.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin guarantee better rankings?

No. The plugin helps with content analysis, structured workflows, internal linking and AI-assisted optimization. Search ranking depends on many factors outside the plugin.

Does the plugin guarantee Google rich results?

No. The schema tools help prepare eligible structured data and identify missing fields. Google decides whether rich results appear.

Does the plugin send content to an external service?

Only connected features send data to the Blue Editoria : Content workflow service, such as service account checks, credit balance, usage history and AI generation requests. Local admin screens and cached analysis data are handled inside WordPress unless a connected feature is triggered. Before the first connected request, an administrator must confirm the external-service disclosure shown on the account screen.

Can I use it without an AI service account?

Yes. A service account is not required to activate the plugin. Local organization, configuration and analysis workflows can be used without remote AI generation. Features that require remote AI processing, account status, usage history or credits require a configured service account because the processing happens on the documented external service.

Does the plugin modify my theme?

No. The plugin does not write to theme files. Generated or assisted outputs are stored through WordPress data structures and plugin options.

Does it work with ACF, JetEngine, Yoast SEO or Rank Math?

The plugin detects supported WordPress fields and common SEO fields when available. It does not create or modify third-party plugin fields automatically.

Is it compatible with multilingual sites?

The plugin includes language-aware organization for multilingual workflows. Internal linking should be managed by language to avoid mixing pages from different languages.
sections.changelog:
1.3.6

  • Reorganizes the WordPress admin navigation into clearer content, linking, campaign and settings groups.
  • Adds persistent progressive accordions and compact secondary-action menus across dense admin screens.
  • Improves campaign, duplicate-content, linking and log layouts on desktop, tablet and mobile.
  • Clarifies active navigation states and keeps one primary action visible in operational tables.

1.3.1

  • Synchronizes the auto-recharge preference with the central Blue Editoria service using the validated REST contract.
  • Keeps the local account state aligned with the server billing snapshot.

1.3.0

  • Centralizes all service, account, pricing, credit and legal URLs on blue-editoria.com.
  • Adds universal credit estimates and configurable spending safeguards before remote AI actions.
  • Adds explicit external-service consent, richer usage receipts and connection diagnostics.
  • Keeps all local plugin features available when the external AI service is not connected.

1.2.9

  • Ajoute une estimation des crédits avant le lancement d’une campagne.
  • Recalcule l’estimation en direct selon les sujets, contenus, champs et longueurs sélectionnés.
  • Affiche une fourchette indicative avant chaque demande envoyée à l’assistant éditorial.
  • Signale lorsque le solde disponible semble insuffisant, sans remplacer le débit réel du service.

1.2.8

  • Synchronisation du solde, de l’offre active et des promotions avec le service Blue Editoria.
  • Affichage du tarif effectif et des crédits inclus dans Mon compte.
  • Conservation de la facturation éditoriale à un crédit par mot et des analyses selon les tokens réellement utilisés.

1.2.7

  • Adds explicit word-based billing context for editorial generation: one generated word equals one credit.
  • Adds token-based billing context for assistants, audits and suggestions: 100 actual tokens equal one credit.
  • Records the billing basis, generated words, tokens and policy version in local usage history.
  • Prevents duplicate local usage rows and removes estimated fallback debits.
  • Aligns campaign credit estimates with the requested output length.

1.2.6

  • Added adaptive internal-link goals for articles, service pages and pillar pages.
  • Added inbound-link distribution and anchor-diversity diagnostics with precise recommendations.
  • Improved duplicate and cannibalization review with language, taxonomy, intent and SEO metadata comparisons.
  • Added non-destructive canonical and merge-review decisions with history snapshots.
  • Added AIOSEO conflict detection and CollectionPage schema for taxonomy archives.
  • Added required Schema.org field validation, a global schema status dashboard and safe bulk repair.

1.2.5

  • Adds cached HTTP health checks for external links with distinct broken, redirected, restricted and unchecked states.
  • Adds an operational link cleanup screen with bulk actions, protected-zone safeguards and rollback history.
  • Invalidates stale linking suggestions after content, custom-field, taxonomy, language or slug changes.
  • Improves suggestion transparency with relevance scores and plain-language reasons.
  • Stops treating published internal pages outside the analyzed scope as broken links.

1.2.4

  • Adds complete editorial assistant reset with confirmation and server-side conversation cleanup.
  • Hides taxonomy enrichment controls outside taxonomy campaigns.
  • Keeps all campaign subsections collapsed by default.
  • Improves generation statistics cards across desktop, tablet and mobile.

1.2.3

  • Moves the campaign summary to a dedicated final verification step.
  • Adds compact accordion subsections throughout the campaign workflow.
  • Reorganizes content selection into existing content, topics and editorial assistant.
  • Simplifies the editorial assistant panel and field-production sections.

1.2.2

  • Removes the campaign recommended-configuration controls.
  • Makes the latest requested topic count authoritative across assistant messages and the saved conversation state.
  • Adds a strict editorial completion pass when the AI returns fewer usable topics than requested.
  • Simplifies the editorial assistant into one chat surface with contextual topic actions.

1.2.1

  • Moves the connected service, account, credits, shop and support links to blue-editoria.com.
  • Migrates stored official service URLs from the previous host without retaining a network fallback.

1.2.0

  • Adds persistent editorial assistant conversations for campaign drafts and saved campaigns.
  • Keeps a separate structured campaign state so recent user corrections override older assumptions.
  • Displays credits charged and the remaining AI balance after each assistant response.
  • Adds explicit actions to append or replace proposed topics and a control to stop a pending browser request.
  • Improves strict handling of platform, language, content type and requested topic-count corrections.

1.1.1

  • Made the topic assistant follow the latest user correction before saved prompts or scanned-site context.
  • Added strict platform and language validation with an automatic corrective pass for off-topic suggestions.
  • Removed the redundant campaign quick-start and top summary blocks for a lighter campaign screen.

1.1.0

  • Added persistent, live-updated activity tracking for site scans, linking scans and campaign generation.
  • Improved campaign state reliability, including completed-with-errors, pause, resume and retry visibility.
  • Reduced admin polling work by loading only active campaigns.
  • Kept campaign generation running in the background while showing service waits and actionable errors.

1.0.8

  • Simplified campaign creation UX with a clearer essential step, optional existing-content selection, and collapsible field instructions.
  • Clarified native WordPress field labels and improved custom-field guidance for AI/manual generation.

1.0.7

  • Added a dedicated taxonomy campaign input for terms, parent terms and briefs so taxonomy campaigns no longer rely on the post topics workflow.

1.0.6

  • Improved campaign target switching so taxonomy campaigns no longer display post/CPT-only fields in the main configuration step.

1.0.1

  • Improved the activity center with clearer progress for scans, campaigns, linking quality and duplicate checks.
  • Strengthened existing-content campaign selection so the chosen post type and language are enforced.
  • Added more actionable internal linking dashboard counters and shortcuts.

1.0.0

  • Renamed public plugin identity to Blue Editoria : Content workflow.
  • Prepared WordPress.org readme, GPL metadata and external service disclosure.
  • Added content analysis, internal linking, spreadsheet-style workflows, schema helpers, multilingual organization, diagnostics and documentation screens.
